title: Customer feedback: tool calling + streaming confusions (Solutions Engineering notes)
content:
Context
- Goal of this doc: capture recurring confusion patterns we’re seeing in customer/prospect conversations around (a) tool calling, (b) tool calling while streaming, and (c) how tool calls relate to structured output.
- This is intentionally “rough notes” from Solutions Engineering (SE) + Support escalations; intended input to DevEx/docs refresh work.
- Scope: Hosted API users primarily; also relevant to Dedicated users doing agentic workflows.

Primary sources / signal
- SE calls + email follow-ups (notably AcmeAI deep dive)
- Support tickets and help-channel questions where examples were copy/paste but still failed
- Observed issues when customers adapt OpenAI examples and expect identical payload/stream events

What customers are trying to do (high-level)
1) Stream assistant output to UI while simultaneously letting the model trigger tools.
2) Run multiple tools in parallel (e.g., search + db lookup) and then provide results back to the model.
3) Force “valid JSON” output (schema constrained) while still using tools.
4) Make the above robust: retries, disconnects, partial tool args, deterministic parsing.

Recurring confusion patterns (ranked by frequency)

1) “Tool call arguments are truncated / invalid JSON mid-stream” (streaming deltas)
What they expect
- A single tool_call event with complete JSON args.
What happens in reality
- Args arrive as incremental deltas. Customers attempt to parse JSON on every delta, hit parse errors, and assume Redwood is sending broken JSON.
- Even when final JSON is valid, intermediate fragments are not.
Symptoms
- “Unexpected end of JSON input” errors
- Customer logs show tool arguments like '{"query": "san fran' mid-stream
- UI code tries to render tool args as soon as they appear
Suggested doc tweak
- Add an explicit callout: “Do not parse tool arguments until the tool call is complete.”
- Provide canonical accumulation logic: collect argument fragments by (tool_call_id) until “tool_call.complete” or final message.
- In streaming docs: show a minimal helper that buffers tool arg deltas + validates at completion.
Notes
- This aligns with SUP-18421. We should quote it in Known Pitfalls with a 3-step fix (buffer → validate → execute).

2) Confusion about event taxonomy: “delta vs message vs done”
What they expect
- The model streams “text tokens” only.
What happens
- Stream includes multiple event types: content deltas, tool call deltas, and final assembled message. Customers treat all events as content.
Symptoms
- Tool call JSON ends up concatenated into chat transcript in UI.
- Customers miss tool calls entirely because they only listen for content tokens.
Suggested doc tweak
- Put a table at top of streaming guide with 4–6 event types and “what you do with it.”
- Add explicit “UI rendering” guidance: render content deltas; do not render tool call deltas; log tool call deltas at debug.
- Include a single “message assembly” reference function in each SDK sample.

3) Misunderstanding of tool calling semantics: “Does Redwood call my function automatically?”
Pattern
- Many users still think tools are like plugins: model “invokes” and Redwood executes on their behalf.
- They miss that tool calling is a protocol: model emits a tool call → client executes tool → client sends tool_result → model continues.
Symptoms
- They define tools and then wait; no tool execution happens.
- They expect tool results to appear in output automatically.
Suggested doc tweak
- Add one diagram (even ASCII) and a short numbered loop:
  1) send messages + tool defs
  2) model returns tool_call(s)
  3) you execute tool(s)
  4) you send tool_result message(s)
  5) model returns final assistant content
- In quickstart, label the loop “Your code runs here” around tool execution.

4) Parallel tool calls: “How do I return results if model calls multiple tools at once?”
What they expect
- A single tool at a time.
What happens
- Some models emit N tool calls in one turn. Customers either:
  - execute only the first tool call
  - execute sequentially but send results with wrong ids
  - send a single aggregated tool_result that doesn’t match expected shape
Symptoms
- Model repeats the same tool call
- Model claims it didn’t receive results
Suggested doc tweak
- Add a “parallel tool calls” section with:
  - stable tool_call_id requirement
  - send one tool_result per tool_call_id
  - ordering guidance: results can be sent in any order but must match ids
- Provide an example with 2 tools called in one model turn.

5) OpenAI-compat assumptions: “Why doesn’t your tool call payload match OpenAI’s exactly?”
Pattern
- Customers copy OpenAI snippets verbatim and then adapt variable names but keep the same conditional branches.
- They assume the stream payload includes the exact same nesting, field names, and “finish_reason” semantics.
Symptoms
- Example code compiles but never detects tool calls
- TypeScript users get type mismatches and work around by “as any,” then runtime break
Suggested doc tweak
- Prominent note early in docs: “Redwood is OpenAI-compatible for many request/response shapes, but tool calling + streaming have documented differences.”
- Link to a compatibility page; include “if you’re porting from OpenAI, watch these 3 differences.”

6) Structured output vs tool calling: “If I use schema-constrained output, do I still need tools?”
Pattern
- Users conflate tools and structured output; they try to use structured output to get the model to output ‘{"tool": ..., "args": ...}’ and then manually execute.
- They don’t understand the trade: structured output is for final data; tools are for side effects + retrieval.
Suggested doc tweak
- Add guidance:
  - Use tools when you need side effects (DB writes, API calls) or retrieval.
  - Use structured output when you need a machine-parseable final answer.
  - You can combine them, but the structured output usually belongs in the final assistant message after tool results.

7) Error handling + retries: “What happens if my stream disconnects while a tool call is in progress?”
Pattern
- Customers have production UI timeouts and reconnect logic. They’re unsure whether to re-run tool executions.
Symptoms
- Duplicate tool execution (double charges, duplicate side effects)
- Stuck agent loops when tool results don’t match the model’s expectation
Suggested doc tweak
- Add a “safe retries” callout:
  - tools should be idempotent where possible
  - persist tool_call_id + args hash; if retried, reuse prior result if same tool_call_id/args
  - if uncertain, restart the turn with a user-visible recovery message

Representative customer/prospect quotes (paraphrased)
- “We see the tool args stream in as half a JSON object. Are you guys sending invalid JSON?”
- “Do I have to parse deltas myself? I assumed the SDK would just give me the final tool call.”
- “Our UI printed the tool call JSON in the chat bubble. We didn’t know it was a separate event.”
- “The model called two tools and then ignored one of the results. Do results need to be in a special order?”
- “We ported our OpenAI agent and it compiles, but tool calls never trigger.”

Suggested documentation changes (actionable edits)

A) Add a short ‘Known pitfalls’ section to Tool Calling + Streaming pages
Must include
- partial tool args during streaming (buffering)
- parallel tool calls (multiple ids)
- do not parse incremental JSON
- do not render tool deltas to UI
- OpenAI-compat differences link

B) Make examples explicitly show “assembly” + “execution loop”
- Every language example should have 3 clearly labeled parts:
  1) define tools (schema + description)
  2) streaming consumer loop (switch on event type)
  3) tool execution + tool_result send back
- If we only show the happy path, customers implement the wrong control flow.

C) Put ‘tool_call_id’ front and center
- Many examples hide ids. Customers then make up their own ids or ignore them.
- We should treat tool_call_id as the join key between tool_call and tool_result.

D) Add copy/paste helper functions per SDK (examples-only)
- parseToolArgsBuffered(toolCallDeltaStream) style helper (name varies by language)
- validate JSON against schema at completion
- small log helpers with recommended log lines (debug vs info)

E) Clarify tool result message shape
- Customers consistently ask: “Do tool results go in role=tool? or role=assistant?”
- Add a single canonical snippet showing tool_result message structure with fields explained.

SDK-specific friction notes

Python
- Customers often iterate stream events but forget to accumulate state; they print event objects and assume “final” will appear.
- Proposed: example should show a state object (current_text, tool_calls_by_id, done flag).

TypeScript
- Biggest pain is typing + unions; many users cast to any.
- Proposed: provide a discriminated union for stream events in examples (even if SDK already has it, show it).
- Also: show runtime validation for tool args (zod/valibot) because TS types alone don’t protect at runtime.

Go
- Users are comfortable with explicit loops but need a clear “where do I store partial args?” answer.
- Proposed: provide a small map keyed by tool_call_id that stores args buffer.

Implementation / rollout suggestions
- Put one canonical sequence diagram (docs) and ensure the same diagram appears in quickstart README.
- Ensure that the first tool-calling example customers see is not “toy-only.” Include parallel tool calls or at least mention it.
- Add a compatibility callout box: “Porting from OpenAI? Read this first.”

Open questions we keep getting (that docs should answer)
1) “Can the model emit both content and a tool call in the same turn?” (Answer: yes; handle both; don’t assume mutual exclusivity.)
2) “Can tool args be non-JSON?” (Answer: treat as string deltas; examples should assume JSON and validate, but note models can misbehave.)
3) “How do I force the model to always call a tool?” (Answer: prompt + tool choice policy; docs should show recommended pattern and caution against hard forcing on weak models.)
4) “Are tool calls guaranteed to be schema-valid?” (Answer: no absolute guarantee across all models; buffer + validate; retry on invalid.)

Action items (suggested owners)
- DevEx/docs: incorporate ‘Known pitfalls’ callouts and event table into streaming guide (Wei Chen + Elliot Price).
- SDK parity: ensure examples use identical conceptual loop + naming across languages (Ibrahim Khan).
- Examples: add parallel tool call sample and include idempotency note (Renee Sullivan).
- Support enablement: update macro / canned response linking to pitfalls section for truncated args + JSON parse issues (Priya Shah + Dev Patel).

Notes to self
- When we publish updated docs, we should proactively message customers/prospects who hit SUP-18421 / SUP-18436 with a short “here’s the new canonical sample + what changed.”
- SE should add 2 questions to discovery calls for agentic workflows:
  - “Are you streaming to UI?”
  - “Do your tools have side effects (writes)?” If yes, bring up idempotency + retries early.
